questions.stem: How is Data Liberalisation related to Data Democratisation?
options: Data Liberalisation replaces Data Democratisation
Data Liberalisation is ideally a prerequisite for Data Democratisation
Data Liberalisation is a tool used after Data Democratisation is complete
Data Liberalisation applies only to unstructured data
The two have nothing to do with each other
questions.explanation: The key phrase is that Data Liberalisation ideally is a prerequisite for Data Democratisation; the two work together and are often confused.

options: Removing all access controls from data
Selling data to third parties
Deleting data that is no longer needed
Providing data in such a way that it is reusable by users
Storing data in a single central database
questions.explanation: Data Liberalisation is about providing data in such a way that it should be reusable by users, whatever the format.

questions.stem: Which are given as examples of the formats through which liberalised data can be provided?
options: Via an API, via BI tools, or via DaaS
Only via printed reports
Only via email attachments
Only via a data warehouse
Only via spreadsheets
questions.explanation: Liberalised data can be in any format, for example via API, via BI tools or via Data as a Service.

questions.stem: When Data Democratisation aims for data access availability for everyone, what does that NOT mean?
options: That data should be reusable
That users can ask analytical questions
That the fear factor about data should be removed
That users can raise questions about data
That everything is shown to everyone without access control
questions.explanation: Data access availability for everyone does not mean showing everything; access is still governed by access control.

questions.stem: What does Data Liberalisation complete the cycle to make sure of?
options: That data is deleted after use
That only IT can access data
That whatever a user accesses is usable rather than a pile of junk data
That data is stored in the cloud
That every report is approved by management
questions.explanation: Data Liberalisation completes the cycle by making sure that whatever the user accesses is usable for them rather than a pile of junk data.

questions.stem: Can the Data Driven Organisation concept be completed by Data Democratisation alone?
options: Yes, Data Democratisation is sufficient on its own
No, Data Liberalisation is also a very crucial component
Yes, as long as a BI tool is purchased
No, it also requires outsourcing analytics
Yes, provided the IT department approves
questions.explanation: The Data Driven Organisation concept cannot be completed just by Data Democratisation; Data Liberalisation is also a very crucial component.

questions.stem: What is the consequence of opening the door of data to everyone when the data is not in a usable format?
options: Users become more data literate
Cultural change is accelerated
Storage costs fall
End users lose confidence and question the integrity of the data, causing greater harm to the organisation
IT receives fewer report requests
questions.explanation: Opening data that is not usable has a negative impact on cultural change: end users lose confidence, question the data's integrity, and the organisation can suffer greater harm.

questions.stem: In a nutshell, what does Data Liberalisation teach about accessibility and usability?
options: Data accessibility is as important as data usability for a Data Driven Organisation
Data accessibility matters far more than usability
Data usability matters only for IT users
Neither accessibility nor usability affects cultural change
Usability can be ignored once data is accessible
questions.explanation: The nutshell statement is that data accessibility is as important as data usability in becoming a Data Driven Organisation.

questions.stem: Why are Data Liberalisation and Data Democratisation described as confusing terms?
options: Because they are both names for a single software product
Because neither has ever been defined
Because they belong to different industries
Because one is about hardware and the other about software
Because they work together and are most of the time mixed with each other
questions.explanation: The two terms are confusing because they work together and are, most of the time, mixed up with each other.

questions.stem: Which of the following is stated as an aim of Data Democratisation?
options: To convert all data to an API format
To limit analytical questions to trained analysts
To remove the fear factor about data
To make data reusable through DaaS
To centralise data ownership in IT
questions.explanation: Data Democratisation aims to remove the fear factor about data, allow everyone to ask analytical questions and have data access availability for everyone.
